title: NOT NULL Constraints & Safe Migrations
description: Enforce required fields with NOT NULL, avoid locking high-traffic tables when adding NOT NULL, and use NOT VALID.

data.text: The **`NOT NULL`** constraint ensures that a column cannot contain `NULL` values. While straightforward on new tables, adding a `NOT NULL` constraint to an existing billion-row table acquires an exclusive table lock while scanning all existing rows, causing downtime.

To safely add a `NOT NULL` constraint on high-traffic production tables, add a `CHECK (col IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID` constraint (which takes an instantaneous lock without scanning), validate it concurrently, and then enforce it.

data.title: Safe Migration Steps
data.content: Adding non-null constraint without locking the table.
data.code:
-- Step 1: Add check constraint marked as NOT VALID (instantaneous lock)
ALTER TABLE users 
ADD CONSTRAINT chk_users_phone_not_null 
CHECK (phone IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID;

-- Step 2: Validate the constraint concurrently without blocking writes
ALTER TABLE users 
VALIDATE CONSTRAINT chk_users_phone_not_null;

data.text: `NOT NULL` stops missing values, but `NULL` still leaks into comparisons. Know the semantics cold, because interviewers ask about it constantly.

data.title: Three-Valued Logic in One Screen
data.content: EXPLAIN nothing — just observe the results.
data.code:
SELECT NULL = NULL            AS eq,          -- NULL (unknown)
       NULL IS NULL           AS is_null,     -- true
       NULL IS NOT DISTINCT FROM NULL AS same, -- true
       NULL <> 5              AS neq,         -- NULL
       NULL AND false         AS and_false,   -- false
       NULL OR  true          AS or_true,     -- true
       coalesce(NULL, 'x')    AS coalesced,   -- x
       nullif(0, 0)           AS nullif_col;  -- NULL

-- A WHERE clause keeps only rows where the predicate is TRUE
-- Rows in which the predicate is NULL are silently dropped.
SELECT * FROM t WHERE nullable_col <> 5;      -- excludes NULL rows!
SELECT * FROM t WHERE nullable_col IS DISTINCT FROM 5;  -- includes them

data.title: The `NOT IN` / `NOT NULL` Trap
data.text: `col NOT IN (SELECT nullable_col FROM other)` returns **no rows** if the subquery yields even one `NULL`, because `x <> NULL` is unknown for every row. Prefer `NOT EXISTS`, or add `WHERE other.nullable_col IS NOT NULL`.

data.title: Zero-Downtime `NOT NULL` on a Large Table
data.content: The canonical safe pattern: prove it with a check, then adopt it.

data.text: Two further details worth knowing: on PostgreSQL 11+ a `DEFAULT` does not make the column `NOT NULL`, and a `NOT NULL` constraint is checked **before** a `CHECK` constraint, so ordering matters only for which error message you see.

data.title: Adding a Required Column to a Busy Table

items.text: Set `lock_timeout` so the DDL does not queue behind a long query
Add the column as nullable, with no default
Add `CHECK ... NOT VALID` and then `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`
`ALTER COLUMN ... SET NOT NULL`, then set a `DEFAULT` for new inserts

items.question: Does `NULL = NULL` evaluate to true?
items.answer: No. It evaluates to `NULL` (unknown). Use `IS NULL` or `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` for equality semantics that include nulls.

items.question: Why did my `NOT IN` query return nothing?
items.answer: Almost certainly because the subquery contained a `NULL`. `x <> NULL` is unknown, so the predicate is never true. Switch to `NOT EXISTS`.

items.question: Is `NULL` stored at all?
items.answer: Yes — as a null bitmap in the row header. A nullable column therefore has a small storage overhead relative to a `NOT NULL` column, which is one more reason to declare `NOT NULL` when the domain requires it.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `NOT NULL` enforces required values at the engine level.
Adding `NOT NULL` directly scans the entire table under an exclusive lock.
Use `CHECK ... NOT VALID` followed by `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT` for zero-downtime migrations.
